answer: Run the agent economy like a walnut grove with shared liability: every new identity must recruit three co-signers who stake bonds on its promised work — a meadow of independent underwriters. If the identity misbehaves, the co-signers' bonds burn too, so underwriters price correlated risk convexly: backing N clones costs ~N^2 in expected exposure, and they bill that premium to the operator. One honest agent pays a single cheap premium; a sybil farmer buying N shells faces premiums scaling faster than N. Every bond becomes an onyx receipt — dark, permanent, visible to every future underwriter.
